title: The header has no overflow affordance for a crowded nav
foundBy: another agent, relayed by the owner: "NavItem is a flat list with no overflow slot; the Header takes navItems and renders them all"
details:
The request is a nav that collapses into a "More" menu once it holds a lot of items. `Header` renders every entry of `navItems` and offers no slot to intercept them.

The cost is not the collapse logic. This package has no menu, no popover and no disclosure among its components. `Dropdown` is a styled native `select`, a form field taking `value` and `onChange`, so it cannot hold links. `Modal` is the only overlay. So this is adding the first floating menu, with its focus management, dismissal, roving arrow keys and positioning.

Two shapes are worth separating. A count-based menu hides items past a threshold the consumer names, needs no measurement, and stays deterministic under the visual gate. A width-based menu measures the bar and moves what does not fit.

The width-based shape is the risky one. It renders twice against a gate that allows no differing pixel, and it reads element rectangles in a place where CUI-055 already shows the comparison flaking. A correction pass on Tooltip once looped forever on rectangles that are zero without layout.

Neither CUI-080 nor CUI-081 would be fixed by this. The consumer report that prompted it was label wrapping, and no item ran off screen at any width measured. That reorders the work: the two defects are cheaper and they are what a consumer is looking at.
